newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FNB HIKES S.AFRICA PRIME RATE TO 20.25 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FNB HIKES S.AFRICA PRIME RATE TO 20.25 PCT.

text.p: First National Bank Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it would lift its prime overdraft rate by one percentage point to 20.25 percent with immediate effect.
The bank said it would also hike its home loan by the same margin to 20.00 percent with immediate effect for new and existing borrowers.
The rate for new fixed interest rate loans would be announced shortly, it said.
"This increase will undoubtedly place the man in the street under further financial pressure," senior general manager for banking, Peter Thompson, said in a statement.
"But we acknowledge that it is inevitable to allow the Reserve Bank to rein in money supply growth, help limit inflation and restrict demand for credit," he added.
FNB is the last of the "big four" banks to hike its prime overdraft rate.
Standard Bank , Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd and Nedcor Ltd all hiked their lending rates by the same margin earlier in the day.
The rate increases come after the Reserve Bank hiked its official lending rate by one point to 17 percent from Thursday.
